name: DunedinPACE (pace of aging)
rangeNote: There's no clinical range. 1.0 is the average pace for a midlife adult: one year of biological aging per calendar year; 0.8 is 20 % slower, 1.2 is 20 % faster. Younger people tend to have lower values and older people higher ones. It comes from a DNA methylation test of a blood sample (an array test from a specialised lab), not from a routine blood test, and the app never calculates it: it records the result your lab reports. Values from different labs or test versions may not match exactly.
summary: How fast your body is aging, estimated from a DNA methylation blood test (DunedinPACE). It was trained to predict how quickly 19 measures of organ health declined over 20 years in people born in Dunedin, New Zealand, in 1972–73.

high.meaning: Above 1.0: faster than the average pace. In studies, faster DunedinPACE was linked with more illness, disability and earlier death. One result is an estimate for a group pattern, not a diagnosis.
commonCauses: Childhood adversity (linked to faster pace in the studies)
Differences between labs or test versions

low.meaning: Below 1.0: slower than the average pace. Younger people tend to have lower values. A lower number doesn't prove that aging was slowed or reversed.
commonCauses: Differences between labs or test versions

sources.title: DunedinPACE, a DNA methylation biomarker of the pace of aging
